newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria's Assad satisfied with Arab backing on peace.
newsitem.headline: Syria's Assad satisfied with Arab backing on peace.

text.p: President Hafez al-Assad on Thursday expressed satisfaction at Arab backing for Syria's terms for resuming peace talks with Israel, his spokesman said on Thursday.
Joubran Kourieh said Assad's remarks were made during a meeting with his deputy Abdel-Halim Khaddam and Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara who briefed him on their tour of North African countries.
"President Assad expressed satisfaction over the outcome of the tour and the talks which were conducted during the tour," Kourieh said.
Khaddam and Shara returned home on Wednesday after delivering messages from Assad to the leaders of Algeria, Mauritania, Morocco, Libya and Tunisia.

A senior Syrian official who accompanied Khaddam said Arab leaders backed Syria's demands that talks with Israel should resume from the point at which they stopped with the previous Labour-led Israeli government.

Syria says the Israeli government that was defeated in elections in May by the Likud party of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had agreed to return all of the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in 1967.
But Netanyahu has rejected trading land for peace, wants to keep the strategic Golan and says talks should begin without any conditions.
A senior official who accompanied Khaddam said the vice-president's tour was mainly aimed at explaining Syria's position.

"The Netanyahu government is trying to deceive the world public openion by pretending that it wants to resume the peace talks with Syria but at the same time Israeli leaders say they want to keep the occupied Syrian lands," the official said.
"If they want to keep the Golan which is Syrian land what are we going to discuss or negotiate with the Israelis," he asked.

"If the current Israeli government wants peace it should honour all the agreements which were reached with the previous Israeli government...it should respect the principles on which the whole peace process is based," he added.
"If we are going to restart from the begining whenever the Israeli government changes there would be no talks and there would be no trust of any Israeli government," the official said.
The official said Khaddam had received the same backing in earlier visits to Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman, Bahrain, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and Yemen.
The last negotiations between Syria and Israel broke off in March after a wave of Islamic suicide bombings in Israel that killed 59 people.
Hopes for a resumption of Syrian-Israeli peace talks revived after Israel and the Palestinians reached a deal on Israeli redeployment in the West Bank city of Hebron last month.
